title: Direct and Indirect Speech: Requests and Orders — Quiz 133
content:
## Direct and Indirect Speech: Requests and Orders

Choose the correct infinitive when reporting an instruction or a negative instruction.

### Lesson focus

1. The govt guidelines said, “Wear mask to beat Covid 19.”
2. Mother said, “Children, don't watch late night horror movies.”

### Understand the pattern

Report an instruction with tell, order or ask plus a listener and a to-infinitive. For a negative instruction, use not to. Choose a reporting verb that matches the tone; do not turn a polite request into a command without reason.

### Worked answers and explanation

The guidelines instructed people to wear masks. Mother told the children not to watch late-night horror films. These are reports of the instructions in the exercise, rather than current health advice. Not belongs before to watch.

### Try another

Report: The teacher said to us, 'Do not run in the corridor.'

### Suggested answer

The teacher told us not to run in the corridor. Told requires the listener us, followed by not to and the base verb run.
